short: The last khagan to rule a united empire; his death in Sichuan broke it apart for good.
full:
Möngke was a son of Tolui and had ridden with Batu in Europe. With Batu's backing he was elected khagan on 1 July 1251, taking the throne from the house of Ögedei; the purge that followed killed a large part of the Ögedeid and Chagatayid aristocracy and settled the succession on Tolui's line. He then audited the empire — a new census, a reformed tax system, curbs on the princes' right to issue their own paiza — and set his brothers to work.

Hulagu was sent west, and destroyed the Assassins of Alamut and the Abbasid Caliphate. Kublai was sent against the Song, and Möngke joined him, invading Sichuan in 1258. The offensive stalled at Diaoyu fortress above the Jialing River, and on 11 August 1259 Möngke died at its foot, of dysentery or of wounds depending on the source. He left no named heir. The recall of the armies saved Egypt and Syria from Hulagu, and the succession war between Kublai and Ariq Böke ended the unified empire.
